skill.name: ponytail-gain
skill.description: Show ponytail's measured impact as a compact scoreboard: less code, less cost, more speed, from the benchmark medians. One-shot display, not a persistent mode, and not a per-repo number. Trigger: /ponytail-gain, "ponytail gain", "what does ponytail save", "show ponytail impact", "ponytail scoreboard".
skill.summary: Display published Ponytail benchmark medians for code size, cost, and speed without estimating savings for the current repository.
skill.author: dietrichgebert

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around a path and a display example. No evidence found of command execution, exfiltration, or prompt injection in SKILL.md. The instructions prohibit persistent changes and distinguish benchmark claims from repository-specific savings.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 19 uses inline Markdown backticks to format the benchmarks/ source reference. This is documentation, with no executable expression or instruction to run commands.
Line 26 opens a Markdown fence containing only scoreboard text, bars, benchmark percentages, and related skill names. No shell or Ruby code appears.
Line 37 closes the scoreboard Markdown fence, followed by prose forbidding invented repository savings. These backticks delimit documentation rather than execute commands.

content.value_statement: Ponytail benchmark gains can be confused with savings measured in your repository. This skill displays a compact scoreboard and keeps those claims separate.
actual_capabilities: Display a one-shot Ponytail scoreboard when invoked by command or matching phrases.
Show the published code size range of 6-20% relative to the no-skill baseline.
Show the published cost range of 23-53% and speed claim of 3-6 times faster.
Label the figures as benchmark medians covering five tasks and three models.
Point to /ponytail-debt and /ponytail-audit without computing repository savings.
Instruct the assistant to avoid file edits, flag files, and persistent mode changes.
limitations: It displays fixed benchmark claims rather than running benchmarks or calculating new measurements.
It cannot establish savings for the current repository because no comparable unbuilt baseline exists.
The benchmark data and README cited by the skill are not included in the reviewed files.
Repository debt counting and further audits require separate skills that are not included here.

use_cases.title: Review Published Gains
use_cases.description: Display the reported code size, cost, and speed comparisons before considering Ponytail for development work.

use_cases.title: Communicate Benchmark Scope
use_cases.description: Share a compact benchmark summary while making clear that it does not measure team or repository savings.

use_cases.title: Separate Claims From Measurements
use_cases.description: Use the scoreboard as a reference for published claims without presenting it as a fresh evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Show the Scoreboard
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: display the default benchmark scoreboard.

prompt_templates.title: Review the Comparisons
prompt_templates.prompt: Show Ponytail impact with the code size, cost, and speed figures. Label them as published benchmark medians.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: identify each comparison and its benchmark scope.

prompt_templates.title: Keep Repository Claims Separate
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the Ponytail scoreboard for our review. Do not infer savings for this repository or change any files or modes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: use the scoreboard during a repository discussion.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Evaluation Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Display Ponytail benchmark medians with their task and model scope. Keep repository measurements separate and retain the related skill references.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a scoped benchmark reference for a tooling evaluation.

output: Published benchmark medians: five tasks and three models.
Code size: 6-20% of the no-skill baseline, reported as an 80-94% reduction.
Cost: 23-53% of the no-skill baseline, reported as a 47-77% reduction.
These figures are not measurements of your repository.

output_examples.input: Show Ponytail impact for this repository.
output: The Ponytail scoreboard reports published benchmark medians, not savings measured in this repository.
No repository savings number is provided because there is no comparable unbuilt baseline.
Related skills: /ponytail-debt for deferred shortcuts and /ponytail-audit for further reduction opportunities.

best_practices: Keep the benchmark scope and baseline visible whenever sharing the figures.
Check the upstream benchmark data before using the claims in purchasing or performance decisions.
Use separate repository measurements when evaluating actual project outcomes.
anti_patterns: Presenting benchmark percentages as measured savings for the current repository.
Treating the fixed scoreboard as a fresh benchmark run or a guaranteed outcome.
Changing files or enabling persistent modes when displaying the scoreboard.

faq.question: How do I invoke the skill?
faq.answer: Use /ponytail-gain or phrases such as 'ponytail gain', 'show ponytail impact', or 'ponytail scoreboard'.

faq.question: What do the benchmark figures cover?
faq.answer: The skill describes five everyday tasks tested with Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus. It labels the displayed figures as published benchmark medians.

faq.question: Does it calculate savings for my repository?
faq.answer: No. It explicitly prohibits repository savings estimates because there is no comparable unbuilt baseline.

faq.question: Does it run benchmarks or execute commands?
faq.answer: No benchmark runner or executable command is included. The instructions request a one-shot display.

faq.question: Does it modify files or change modes?
faq.answer: The instructions prohibit file edits, flag files, and persistent mode changes.

faq.question: Were the benchmark claims independently verified in this review?
faq.answer: No. Only SKILL.md was available for review; the referenced benchmark data and README were not included.
